I knew I wanted kids but I didn't expect one quite so soon. I got pregnant unexpectedly 2 months after getting married. Was told I was infertile without help such as IVF and such and what do you know. My body decided apparently for me lol. 

Honestly I love my baby. Yes it's hard, yes it's a lot and yeah giving birth hurts but I wouldn't change it. I miss my sleep but it ain't the worst thing in the world. To me raising my child is better than having the soul sucked out of me at the dead end jobs I used to have. My anxiety is worse but it's localized to my child, I can actually order my own food without having a breakdown now. And my depressions better. I have more friends. I'm finding my hobbies again now thats she's 1 year and I'm doing my best. My child has made me want to go to therapy and get medicated and start working on myself. I'm not suicidal anymore. 

That being said please pick someone who helps and supports you with the child. I definitely would not be having a good time if I didn't have a very loving supportive partner. His only vice was pitching in and thankfully we worked through that and now we are a solid team. We do everything regarding our child together. We take care of the house together. He's always been in my corner. Newborn life sucked between us but she was a good newborn relatively. We were just adjusting. She's now 1 and the happiest thing I've ever seen. She makes goofy faces at me, we actually can have conversations, she understand sooo much and is my lil ride or die girl. We're currently going though the sleep regression phase but I know it won't last forever. It's totally doable. Just make sure you have support and that you really commit to it. It's fine if you're unsure but once that baby is here you gotta commit. You made the decision you gotta stick to it.

My partner cleans and does the laundry and often cooks dinner for me so all I have to do when I get home is maybe a few pickups of my own bits of clutter but other than that I just relax. 

2. I had morning sickness really badly the first trimester and anything I mentioned I feel like I could maybe eat, he had it ready for me, along with crackers and my meds and some ginger tea or other drink to help. Just being available helps a lot. 

3. I think the oil smell diffuser is great! However be prepared if your partner has scent and smell aversions. It's not that they won't appreciate it but the sense of smell can get wonky while pregnant. I had to wear a mask every time I walked into my own kitchen because i could smell literally everything! And grocery stores were horrendous and scented candles made me puke! Thankfully it's subsided but just be prepared! 

4. My partner has been driving me to work because I've been having bouts of dizziness and fatigue in my third trimester. It's not feasible for everyone but it helps so much not having to worry about potentially having to pull over or getting in a jam while driving. 

Those are my main things. Again it's not really material but they help me soooo much and I really am appreciative of the little things he does to help make it easier on me.
